data.name: AEGYPTUS
data.detailed_description:
A game inspired on Egyptian mythology, consist of two different gameplay types, finished the survival-style open world game map and complete the objectives to access the various pyramids where the gameplay changes radically, explores the various dungeons and survive traps. Find the exit and seals the various pyramids to escape from Egyptian gods who try in every way to block you and keep you from escaping away..



Aegyptus is an open world adventure with elements of survival and enigmas, climatic events and a totally hand-drawn story with comics, you're alone in the desert and you have to find a way to escape, search for water springs for not dehydrate yourself, find a way to enter the pyramid and you'll be catapulted into an Egyptian dungeon where in addition to avoid deadly traps you have to escape from anubis fury, the game proposes three totally different gameplay styles alternating: survival, deadly dungeons Full of mortal traps and escape.



. The desert, a huge freely explored borderless map (Completed)
. Day night cycle in real time (Completed)
. First part of the story hand drawn on paper (Completed)
. Rain climatic event that affects the gameplay (water sources fill in during rains but exhaust with the heat of the desert) (Completed)
. Possibility to change visuals between first and third person (Completed)
. Complete hud with stamina, dehydration, batteries and updated targets (Completed)
. Pause menu with keyboard/gamepad commands (actually not configurable) (Completed)
. Over 50 sounds made for the actions of the main character and nice sound for the desert and dungeon atmosphere (Completed)
. 8 complete puzzles (Completed)
. Footprints in real-time terrain so as not to get lost in the desert (Completed)
. Torch to be charged with batteries to fight the night (Completed)
. Titans(giant worms) (Completed)
. First dungeon (Completed)



Currently aegyptus is in the prealpha version and I am working on content that will be released gradually through future patches to make gaming experience even more immersive and addictive.



. Steam emoticons
. 3 dungeons within their respective pyramids with over 20 different types of traps (Work in progress)
. A lot of original hand-made paper designs that will tell the story's evolution and will also be incorporated into gameplay (Work in progress)
. 2 Egyptians boss(anubis and horus) trying to stop at some parts of the dungeons (Work in progress)
. Quick time events in certain sections of the game (Work in progress)
. Steam achievements (Work in progress)
. Steam cards (Work in progress)

Some of these things may change or be modified during project development

reviews.review:
For a second project of this developer (the first one being [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/377980/Mortos/]Mortos[/url]), AEGYPTUS shows a lot of potential. However it does need a great amount of work still in order to not be catalogued as a "bad game".

In its current Early Access state, there are only two levels available. Figuring out the levels takes quite some effort, but a speedrun would only require a few minutes. As opposed to the  first level, which offers more of a walking simulator / exploration with light puzzle elements kind of gameplay, the second one is a huge obstacle race inside a labyrinth with unlit corridors. On top of that there's the survival layer, present in both levels: the player needs to reach a water source every few minutes, otherwise they die.

While the second level is quite dynamic and rather frustrating (since there's a lot of trial and error, in order to learn the locations, the right corridors and all the traps), the first seems a bit blunt and lacking content. One spends most of the time running aimlessly through the desert trying to find either a source of water or "something", and it is not clear from the beginning what items one is supposed to search for. However, completing these mini-objectives is rewarded with a very nicely drawn black and white comic panel.

Playing the game in motion doesn't look as nice as in the store screenshots, where the perspectives are artistically selected to flatter. In practice, the movement of the character is shaky (he walks a bit like a robot, swinging to the left and right). The graphics often clip and the menacing sand worm from the first level seems to weirdly sink underground, instead of progressively burying itself in the sand. The player character can look down at his body and goatee, and occationally even those unexpectedly clip into view.

The movement speed is dreadful and not even pressing the sprint button could help the player character win a race against a 100 years old turtle. Sprinting consumes stamina very quickly, and having to wait for it to recharge every few seconds is quite annoying.

The whole UI could use some touching up and maybe a redesign with the help of an artistic eye. For example, the menu panels seem to be constructed as layers glued on top of each other, but they are not precisely assembled, leaving some extra space on the border that shouldn't be there. The font selected has an Egyptian nuance, but in practice it's very hard to read, especially when one is not used to it yet.

On the other hand, AEGYPTUS is a collection of several funny-crazy elements: there are alien spinning buildings, mysterious prehistoric statues, ancient Egyptian temple pillars, huge stone balls rolling at you, spike traps, disappearing platforms etc. It's a weird mix, but it gives a unique flavor to the game.

So… why a positive review after so many complaints? Because AEGYPTUS seems to have a bunch of nice ideas (yet in its current state, it needs a great amount of polishing). It's on the right path, but not there quite yet. Though I am hopeful that it will improve a lot in the future.
